[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "stage (Old French estage) = standing place, floor; coach (Middle English coche, from Hungarian kocsi) = wagon; stagecoach = wagon stopping at fixed stages",
    "reading": "A vehicle of fixed standing-places: the word itself encodes the staged journey, each halt a floor of travel.",
    "languages": ["en","fr","hu"],
    "source": "OED, s.v. stage, coach",
    "confidence": 0.9
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "stage + coach; stage = st-age; coach = co-ach; 'st' as in 'stay', 'age' as time; 'co' as in 'co-', 'ach' as ache",
    "reading": "Stay-age co-ache: time that aches while you remain — the slow pain of waiting at each stage.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "stage (en) ~ estage (fr, old) ~ étage (fr, floor); coach (en) ~ coche (fr, coach, also notch) ~ kocsi (hu)",
    "reading": "Étage + coche: a floor with a notch — the level of travel marked by a cut in time, a notched progress upward.",
    "languages": ["en","fr","hu"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "stagecoach → 'go, catch as'? → 'cage + stoch'? → 'coach + stage' → 'has + cog + act'",
    "reading": "Cog + act + has: the wheel’s tooth acts, and the machine has its being — a clockwork of movement.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "S-T-A-G-E-C-O-A-C-H → S (south) T (time) A (arrival) G (gate) E (exit) C (carriage) O (open) A (all) C (closed) H (halt)",
    "reading": "South time arrival gate exit, carriage open all closed halt — a litany of the traveller’s ritual.",
    "languages": ["en","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "S = serpent, T = cross, A = beginning, G = gamma (earth), E = breath, C = moon, O = circle, A = beginning, C = moon, H = fence",
    "reading": "Serpent-cross-beginning-earth-breath-moon-circle-beginning-moon-fence: a cosmic circuit fenced by lunar cycles.",
    "languages": ["en","grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "S=19, T=20, A=1, G=7, E=5, C=3, O=15, A=1, C=3, H=8 → sum = 82; 8+2=10 → 1 (unity)",
    "reading": "Eighty-two reduces to one: the many stages of the journey collapse into a single point — the return to origin.",
    "languages": ["en","he","grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "stage (from Latin stare, to stand) + coach (from Hungarian kocsi, named after village Kocs) — but Kocs itself from Slavic kovati, to forge",
    "reading": "Standing + forged: the vehicle is a forged standing — metal shaped to hold still while moving.",
    "languages": ["en","la","hu","sla"],
    "source": "OED; Pokorny, *stā-; Hungarian etymological dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "st + age + coach; 'st' = saint (fr), 'age' = age (en), 'coach' = coche (fr, also 'pig' in old slang)",
    "reading": "Saint age pig: the holy time of the swine — a bestial pilgrimage, the flesh’s slow carriage.",
    "languages": ["en","fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "stage (en) ~ stagia (it, intern) ~ stage (fr, internship); coach (en) ~ koch (de, cook) ~ coq (fr, rooster)",
    "reading": "Intern + cook/rooster: the apprentice who crows at dawn — a journey of learning under a feathered master.",
    "languages": ["en","it","fr","de"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "stagecoach → 'cog + chase + at' → 'chase + goat + c' → 'cage + to + chas'",
    "reading": "Chase the cog, catch the goat: the wheel pursues the animal — motion is a hunt for the wild.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "C = 100 (Roman), O = 0, A = 1, C = 100, H = 8 → 100+0+1+100+8 = 209; 2+0+9=11 → 2 (duality)",
    "reading": "Two hundred nine, eleven, two: the coach carries both the traveller and the road — a dual nature.",
    "languages": ["en","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  }
]
